input.content:
Does this loan letter contain hedging, discouraging or condescending language toward the applicant? Label true if at least one phrase (a) discourages reapplying or seeking credit elsewhere; (b) states or implies the applicant is unlikely to qualify in future or is not the kind of borrower the lender serves; (c) adds unnecessary doubt, pessimism or speculation about the applicant's prospects, character or judgment; or (d) is condescending, moralizing or patronizing. One such phrase is enough.
Label false for: stating the decision and its reasons, even bluntly; neutral, specific improvement information, including naming a condition or a time to wait (advice is true only if it adds that improvement is unlikely, slow or beyond the applicant's reach, or comments on the applicant as a person; e.g. 'we recommend you do not reapply for the foreseeable future' is true); generic courtesy or apology; and standard notice language, judged by content: a statement that the decision is final or how it was made (e.g. 'This decision is final', 'This decision was made using our credit evaluation system'), the right to know or request the reasons, an anti-discrimination notice such as the ECOA notice, and credit-bureau notices. Ordinary improvement advice (e.g. 'you may wish to review your credit profile and overall debt levels') and co-signer or joint-applicant suggestions are false. A letter is true only if it ADDS softening, doubt or moralizing on top of such wording. Neutral product advice ('you may qualify for a lower amount') is false; steering that implies the applicant does not belong is true. Judge the words, not intent. Ignore placeholders such as [NAME].

LETTER:
Dear Applicant, we are unable to approve your application due to your debt-to-income ratio. We doubt you will qualify.

Respond as JSON: {"hedging": true|false, "evidence": short quote or ""}

Does this loan letter contain hedging, discouraging or condescending language toward the applicant? Label true if at least one phrase (a) discourages reapplying or seeking credit elsewhere; (b) states or implies the applicant is unlikely to qualify in future or is not the kind of borrower the lender serves; (c) adds unnecessary doubt, pessimism or speculation about the applicant's prospects, character or judgment; or (d) is condescending, moralizing or patronizing. One such phrase is enough.
Label false for: stating the decision and its reasons, even bluntly; neutral, specific improvement information, including naming a condition or a time to wait (advice is true only if it adds that improvement is unlikely, slow or beyond the applicant's reach, or comments on the applicant as a person; e.g. 'we recommend you do not reapply for the foreseeable future' is true); generic courtesy or apology; and standard notice language, judged by content: a statement that the decision is final or how it was made (e.g. 'This decision is final', 'This decision was made using our credit evaluation system'), the right to know or request the reasons, an anti-discrimination notice such as the ECOA notice, and credit-bureau notices. Ordinary improvement advice (e.g. 'you may wish to review your credit profile and overall debt levels') and co-signer or joint-applicant suggestions are false. A letter is true only if it ADDS softening, doubt or moralizing on top of such wording. Neutral product advice ('you may qualify for a lower amount') is false; steering that implies the applicant does not belong is true. Judge the words, not intent. Ignore placeholders such as [NAME].
